intervals.label: development and surface-laboratory commissioning (10-L detector at MIT)
intervals.note: Start year = the earliest DMTPC collaboration paper read (arXiv:0708.2370, August 2007: 'developed by the DMTPC collaboration'); the collaboration's own start is not published. End = the start of the underground run at WIPP (October 2010). The dates of the MIT surface run itself are not stated.
intervals.quote: To study detector backgrounds, a commissioning run was taken in a surface laboratory at MIT.

intervals.label: 10-L detector running underground at WIPP
intervals.note: Start verified (October 2010). Open interval: no source read states when the WIPP run ended or that it continues. The latest DMTPC paper read is arXiv:1705.05965 (2017), a model of directional sensitivity of two DMTPC laboratory detectors; no WIPP dark matter result was found. The 2021 Annual Review (arXiv:2102.04596) describes DMTPC only in the past tense and says 'A 1 m3 detector was constructed, but to our knowledge not deployed'. The collaboration website's last Internet Archive capture is 2019-07-29.
intervals.quote: The 10L detector described here began running underground at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant outside Carlsbad, NM in October 2010. The depth of the WIPP site is 1.6 km water-equivalent.

name: DMTPC 10-liter detector
notes: Records the 10-liter detector (surface run at MIT, then WIPP). The 20-liter and 1 m^3 detectors were only plans or under commissioning in the sources read and are not recorded.

placements.note: Underground run at WIPP; the WIPP site record is a campus-grade surface point (approximate), no underground coordinate of the DMTPC location is published. Open: see the experiment's interval note.
placements.quote: The 10-liter detector has completed a surface run to study backgrounds and is currently deployed underground at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP – near Carlsbad, NM) at a depth of 1600 meters water equivalent.

placements.note: Surface commissioning run (35.7 g d) in a basement laboratory at MIT; campus-grade site only.
placements.quote: To study detector backgrounds, a commissioning run was taken in a surface laboratory at MIT.

active_volume.note: Detector volume of the 10-liter DMTPC prototype (the 20-liter detector was commissioning at MIT in 2010).
active_volume.quote: The Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber (DMTPC) collaboration has developed and operated a 10-liter gas-based directional dark matter detector.

target_mass.note: CF4 target mass of the 10-liter detector at 75 Torr.
target_mass.quote: The current instrument consists of a dual TPC, filled with CF4 gas at 75 Torr (3.3 g target mass).

summary.plain: DMTPC (Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber) is a directional dark matter experiment led from MIT. A low-pressure CF4 gas chamber with camera readout images the tracks of recoiling nuclei, which could reveal the direction a dark matter particle came from. A 10-litre detector ran at MIT and then underground at WIPP.
summary.technical: Low-pressure (75 Torr) CF4 dual back-to-back TPC with CCD (proportional scintillation) and charge readout, 10-liter detector with a 3.3 g CF4 target. MIT surface run (35.7 g d, 80-200 keV): spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 2.0e-33 cm^2 at 115 GeV/c^2 (90% CL). Moved to the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (1.6 km w.e.) in October 2010; a 20-liter detector was commissioned at MIT. 2017: model of the directional response of two detectors at 30-60 torr.

technology.quote: The Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber (DMTPC) is a low pressure (75 Torr CF4) 10 liter detector capable of measuring the vector direction of nuclear recoils with the goal of directional dark matter detection.
technology.value: Low-pressure (75 Torr) CF4 dual back-to-back time projection chamber with CCD optical readout and charge readout
